title: Should You Bring an Iced Coffee to an Interview
paragraphs: For many people, an iced coffee is part of their daily routine. But is it OK to bring one to a job interview? A new survey shows that American workers and human resources (HR) professionals have different opinions.

The survey was carried out in October by SHRM, a large organization for HR professionals in the US. It asked both workers and HR professionals what they think about job candidates who bring an iced coffee to an in-person interview.

Most workers did not like the idea. In total, 56% of workers said it was inappropriate. Of these, 32% said it was definitely inappropriate, and 24% said it was somewhat inappropriate. Only 21% of workers thought it was appropriate, while 23% did not have an opinion.

HR professionals, who often take part in hiring, were more relaxed about it. Half of them said they were neutral. Around 40% said bringing an iced coffee was inappropriate, but only 17% said it was definitely inappropriate.

People who are against the idea say that bringing a drink can make a candidate look too casual for a formal meeting. There are also practical problems. For example, the drink could spill, distract people or make it awkward to shake hands or hold documents.

On the other hand, some people say that coffee is a normal part of many workplaces. They also argue that a drink says nothing about a person's skills or their respect for the company. In addition, rules about how to behave at work are changing, with more relaxed dress codes and different expectations between generations.

So, what should job seekers do? SHRM suggests that it is safer to leave the iced coffee behind, especially when interviewing at a traditional company. For employers, it points out that a candidate's choice of drink may say very little about how well they can do the job.
